output.scope_note: The paper is about Li solid-state battery electrolytes and reports EIS-derived room-temperature ionic conductivities for four of them, alongside NMR relaxation data.

records.evidence_quote: The determined conductivities are 0.75 mS cm-1, 0.66 mS cm-1, 9 × 10-3 mS cm-1 and 2.63 mS cm-1 for LiInCl6, LiYCl6, Li1.48Al0.48Ge1.52(PO4)3 and Li6PS5Cl respectively.
records.notes: Value is from the Figure 2 caption, which names the compound LiInCl6 (the text calls it Li3InCl6). Measurement temperature not stated. The panel labels in Figure 2 are garbled in the text extraction and seem to pair 0.66 with LIC and 0.75 with LYC, which conflicts with the caption order; the caption order was used here.

records.notes: Value is from the Figure 2 caption, which names the compound LiYCl6 (the text calls it Li3YCl6). Measurement temperature not stated. The Figure 2 panel labels conflict with the caption order (see the LIC record).

records.evidence_quote: The determined conductivities are 0.75 mS cm-1, 0.66 mS cm-1, 9 × 10-3 mS cm-1 and 2.63 mS cm-1 for LiInCl6, LiYCl6, Li1.48Al0.48Ge1.52(PO4)3 and Li6PS5Cl respectively.
records.notes: The text says the LAGP pellet was sintered at 700 °C for 12 h in air before EIS and that conductivity rose after sintering, but the caption does not say whether 9 × 10-3 is the sintered or unsintered value. Treat the sintering conditions as applying to this value with some uncertainty. Al is part of the nominal composition, not a substituent added to a parent compound, so dopants is left as Al only by the formula's composition; this may be better empty.
